title: Written revelation is sacred theology's first principle; it is called Sacred Scripture
pass_a_gloss: CHAPTER THREE. On sacred Scripture. I. Written revelation is the first principle of sacred theology referred by the prophets and Apostles into the sacred letters, from which the dogmas of the faith and of the Christian life, and all disputations concerning revealed things, are first deduced, and into which they are last resolved: and in the same sense it is called SACRED SCRIPTURE.
pass_b_english: I. What the prophets and Apostles committed to the sacred letters is written revelation — sacred theology's first principle. From that written deposit the dogmas of the faith and of Christian life are first drawn, and every dispute about revealed things is finally resolved back into it. In that sense we call it Sacred Scripture.
source_text:
CAPUT TERTIUM.
De sacra Scriptura.

I. Scripta revelatio est principium primum S. Theologiae a prophetis & Apostolis in sacras literas relatum, ex quo dogmata fidei vitaeque Christianae, omnesque de rebus revelatis disputationes primo deducuntur, & in quod ultimo resolvuntur: eodemque sensu SACRA SCRIPTURA dicitur.
